treatment: Reduce load on the painful area and avoid any movement that reproduces sharp pain.
Use a structured warm-up and cool-down focused on mobility and tissue prep before dancing.
Apply a warm-up before activity and a cool-down after activity to help tissues adapt gradually.
pt_exercises: Gentle range-of-motion work in a pain-free range.
Single-leg balance drills to improve control and reduce compensation.
Core activation with dead bug or bird dog drills to support alignment.
strengthening: Progressive glute bridge and single-leg bridge work to improve hip stability.
Band-resisted external rotation and isometric holds for control and tendon support.
Calf raises, hamstring curls, and step-downs to build capacity around the lower body.
general.return_to_dance: Progress back into full dancing only when the area feels stable, pain-free during rehearsal, and you can complete technical movement without compensation.

treatment: Protect the ankle from repeated impact and avoid jumping or cutting until the pain has settled.
Use a compression wrap and ice for flare-ups, especially after rehearsals or long dance days.
Focus on mobility in the foot and calf, then gradually reintroduce controlled weight-bearing work.
pt_exercises: Ankle alphabet circles and calf pumps through a pain-free range.
Single-leg balance with toe raises and reach drills.
Gentle posterior chain work such as calf raises and controlled heel-elevated squats.
strengthening: Eccentric calf raises with slow lowering.
Single-leg hip stability work such as step-downs and split squats.
Band-resisted ankle inversion and eversion to improve stability.
ankle.return_to_dance: Return only after you can hop, land, and pivot without pain or wobble, and after your calf and ankle strength have improved.

treatment: Reduce repeated loading and avoid deep knee bends, jumps, and turns until pain is controlled.
Support the knee with a sleeve or wrap if it improves comfort, but prioritize full control and mobility.
Use a structured activation plan for glute and calf muscles so the knee is not overloaded during landing.
pt_exercises: Glute bridge holds with abduction and terminal knee extension drills.
Step-downs and squat-to-chair work with controlled depth.
Single-leg balance and half-squat holds for control.
strengthening: Glute bridges, lateral band walks, and split squats.
Hamstring curls and calf raises to improve leg alignment.
Wall sits or squat holds with a gradual progression in duration.
knee.return_to_dance: Return to impact work gradually after pain-free squatting, step-downs, and controlled landing mechanics are restored.

treatment: Avoid repetitive hip flexor strain positions and reduce loading during kicks or high-range movements.
Keep the pelvis and trunk aligned and avoid overcompensating with your low back or knee.
Use progressive mobility work without forcing end-range hip flexion or extension.
pt_exercises: 70/90 hip flexor stretch variations with a neutral pelvis.
Glute bridge march and clamshell activation.
Side-lying hip abduction and adductor isometrics.
strengthening: Single-leg RDL and glute bridge progressions.
Lateral band walks and open-chain hip abduction.
Split squat and step-up progressions to build control and power.
hip.return_to_dance: Reintroduce kicks and turns after strength and flexibility are restored and the hip no longer compensates during movement.

treatment: Use neutral spine positions, reduce repetitive spinal loading, and avoid high-force turns until symptoms calm down.
Prioritize breathing, core stability, and pelvis control rather than aggressive stretch work.
If there is sharp pain or radiation, avoid pushing through discomfort and seek evaluation.
pt_exercises: Dead bug and bird dog to improve trunk control.
Cat-cow movement and mindful spinal mobility in a pain-free range.
Supine core activation with leg movements while keeping the rib cage down.
strengthening: Good mornings with light resistance and controlled tempo.
Glute bridge progressions and side planks.
Hip hinge and posterior chain strengthening for lower back support.
back.return_to_dance: Return after you can hold posture and perform core-controlled movement without pain, guarding, or low-back fatigue.

treatment: Avoid overhead loading and avoid pushing ranges that cause pinching, sharp pain, or weakness.
Use controlled mobility and scaption work instead of aggressive stretching.
Support posture and scapular control to reduce compensation during upper-body movement.
pt_exercises: Scapular wall slides and shoulder blade retraction drills.
Pendulum swings and controlled shoulder circles.
Isometric external rotation presses against a wall.
strengthening: Band external rotation and row progressions.
Wall push-up plus and serratus activation.
Rotator cuff and scapular stability work with a slow tempo.
shoulder.return_to_dance: Return gradually after overhead movements are pain-free and shoulder stability and scapular control are restored.

treatment: Reduce repetitive forefoot loading and avoid forcing pointe or toe-flexing work until pain settles.
Support the arch and toe position with appropriate footwear or insoles if needed.
Keep the foot moving through a full but pain-free range to reduce stiffness.
pt_exercises: Short foot exercises and toe spreading drills.
Arch raises and controlled mobility work in the metatarsal region.
Gentle exercises for the calf and intrinsic foot muscles.
strengthening: Toe curls, marshmallow foot press, and resisted arch work.
Single-leg calf raises and balance work for dynamic control.
Progressive deep squat holds with proper foot alignment.
foot.return_to_dance: Return when the foot can absorb force under load without pain, and when your arches and intrinsic muscles can stabilize balance.

treatment: Reduce impact load and avoid hard repetitive jumps until the pain has decreased.
Focus on lower-leg mobility and foot mechanics to avoid shin splint symptoms reappearing.
Progress volume gradually and avoid doubling your effort in one rehearsal.
pt_exercises: Calf raises and foot mobility drills.
Gentle stretching of the calf and tibialis muscles.
Single-leg balance and low-impact movement control.
strengthening: Eccentric calf raises and tibialis strengthening.
Band-resisted foot and shin exercises.
Progressive step-ups and landing control drills.
shin.return_to_dance: Return to jumping and fast turns only when the shin tolerates load and your strength and landing mechanics are improved.
